paper.authors_full: Zhiwei Liu, Haode Zuo, Jue Feng, Yongjing Lu
paper.title: Who Is the Best Helper for University Students' Mathematical Creativity? A Quasi‐Experimental Study of Human–ChatGPT, Human–Google, and Human–Human Co‐Creation
paper.pdf_filename: Liu et al (2025) - Who Is the Best Helper for University Students' Mathematical Creativity.pdf
paper.version_read: Published journal version of record: Computer Applications in Engineering Education, 2025; 33:e70100, DOI 10.1002/cae.70100; received 10 July 2025, revised 10 September 2025, accepted 13 October 2025 (PDF p. 1).
paper.one_line_finding: Students working with ChatGPT scored higher than Google users and the peer arm on flexibility (15.03 vs 12.83 and 12.38) and fluency (27.85 vs 23.78 and 23.42), and between them on originality (5.47 vs 3.88 Google and 7.00 peer); three-group F (2, 172) = 9.71, 7.91, and 18.31, Bonferroni p ≤ 0.001, with no pairwise test printed (p. 7, Table 3).
paper.shared_samples: Possible overlap with c471: Liu et al. (2026), Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students' mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study, doi:10.14742/ajet.10564. The c089 ChatGPT arm and c471 experimental arm have identical reported demographics: age M = 19.20, SD = 1.36; male/female 39/21; sciences/liberal arts/engineering 16/16/28; prior ChatGPT experience never/seldom/sometimes/often/always 2/10/24/23/1. They also use the same baseline and four MCT tasks, but their creativity means and SDs differ. Neither full text explicitly confirms shared participants or independence. Reuse and the number of shared people remain unconfirmed; author clarification is needed before treating these samples as independent. Possible overlap does not establish that c089 is a reanalysis.

studies.label: Mathematical creativity tasks with ChatGPT, Google Search, or a human peer

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1-3.2; arm counts also appear in PDF p. 4, Table 1
counts_source.quote: A total of 230 Chinese university students participated in this study. ... the human–ChatGPT group contained 60 participants, the human–Google group contained 60 participants, and the human–human group contained 110 participants (55 dyads).

arms.name: Human–ChatGPT
arms.description: Students used ChatGPT through a single browser tab on identical PCs, with instructions on prompting, refining responses, and uploading images or documents. Web searches were permitted but no participant used them (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Human–Google
arms.description: Students could use Google Search only; other AI tools and search engines were blocked (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

arms.name: Human–human
arms.description: Students worked in 55 randomly formed dyads. Person A led and person B supported without completing independent work. Whether the analyzed creativity scores represent the dyad jointly or the lead student is unspecified; the analyzed-person count remains unconfirmed (PDF p. 3, Sections 3.1-3.2; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1).

studies.task: After an individual number-pyramid baseline, students generated as many solutions as possible to four open-ended mathematical tasks concerning equal-area figures, marble dispersion, water in a tilted prism, and shared properties of geometrical shapes (PDF pp. 3-6, Sections 3.1 and 4.1-4.2; Table 2; Figure 1).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (model version not stated)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1 Procedure; neither a model version nor its release year is stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is reported in the article. PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 reports post hoc power analysis; PDF p. 2, RQ1 names the three creativity outcomes without identifying a primary outcome.

studies.shared_sample: Possible overlap with c471, Liu et al. (2026), Exploring the impact of ChatGPT on college students' mathematical creativity: A quasi-experimental study, doi:10.14742/ajet.10564, as flagged in the reconciled screening form's sample_overlap. Matching ChatGPT-arm demographics and tasks raise the possibility; c089 does not confirm reuse or independence. No shared-person count is established.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Hand-coded number of correct answer categories, summed across the four MCT tasks. Answers were first marked correct or wrong, then categorized by two scorers, with discrepancies resolved. Table 3 reports raw scores; the mixed pre/post ANOVAs instead use z-standardized scores (PDF p. 4, Section 3.3; PDF pp. 6-7, Section 5).

estimates.notes: The Table 3 quotation lists all three arms in printed order: Human–ChatGPT M/SD, Human–Google M/SD, Human–human M/SD. Only the named contrast's means and SDs are extracted. Printed decimal precision is retained in the quotation. Table 3 F statistics, partial eta-squared values, and p-values are three-arm omnibus results. Section 6.1 mixed-ANOVA statistics and within-arm baseline-to-MCT t tests/Cohen's d are not pairwise randomized-arm effects. No pairwise difference, SE, CI, test, p-value, or standardized effect is printed; these fields remain null. No contrast-specific total people count is printed; n_total is not obtained by adding arm counts. Each arm has one summed creativity score per student. The printed arm sizes and the no-exclusions statement (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1) support the analyzed-person counts. sd_level remains participant because the arm SDs describe individual student scores. se_basis is not_reported because the paper reports no sampling uncertainty for this ChatGPT-versus-Google contrast; arm SDs describe score dispersion and do not constitute a reported contrast SE. n_units is null because there is no separate non-person observation count.

not_extracted.what: Within-arm baseline-to-MCT changes in flexibility (all three arms)
not_extracted.reason: The reported paired t tests and Cohen's d compare a solo baseline with a later, different task in fixed order. This is not a randomized-order within-person comparison or a contrast between randomized arms; the solo baseline is not a no-AI control arm (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; PDF p. 4, Section 3.3; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1).

not_extracted.what: Three-arm omnibus ANOVAs and mixed-ANOVA time, condition, and interaction effects for MCT flexibility, fluency, and originality
not_extracted.reason: The F tests, partial eta-squared values, and p-values test all three conditions or the overall time structure. They cannot be assigned to either two-arm AI contrast. The eligible posttest arm means and SDs are extracted separately (PDF p. 7, Table 3, rows 2-4; PDF pp. 7-8, Section 6.1).

not_extracted.what: ANCOVA associations of prior mathematical competence with flexibility, fluency, and originality
not_extracted.reason: The printed tests concern the baseline competence covariate, not adjusted pairwise effects of randomized AI assistance (PDF p. 8, Section 6.1; PDF p. 10, Section 7.2).

not_extracted.what: Exploratory correlations involving actual performance, self-evaluation, perceived partner usefulness, effort, difficulty, and self-efficacy
not_extracted.reason: Associations within conditions and self-report correlations do not estimate randomized AI-arm contrasts. Main-text discussion refers to external Appendix tables that are not on file (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.3-7.5).

not_extracted.what: Human–Google versus Human–human on MCT flexibility, fluency, and originality
not_extracted.reason: Neither arm supplies generative-AI assistance; this is outside the required AI-versus-comparison contrasts (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; PDF p. 7, Table 3).

open_items: The peer-arm analyzed-person count, joint-dyad versus lead-student score mapping, SD level, and handling of individual baseline scores remain unspecified. Overall analyzed-person N is therefore also null (PDF pp. 3-4 and 7-8).

The paper does not print pairwise creativity differences, SEs, CIs, p-values, tests, or standardized effects for ChatGPT versus Google or ChatGPT versus a peer. Omnibus and within-arm statistics cannot fill these fields (PDF pp. 7-8).
Contrast-specific total people counts are not separately printed. They are left null instead of being computed from arm counts.
The ChatGPT model/version and its release year are not stated; ai_tool.year is null (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).

The separate online Supporting Information appendix was not obtained and was not used. The main text identifies scoring-reference tables and exploratory Appendix Tables A1 and A3; other contents and any additional statistics remain unverified (PDF p. 6, Section 5; PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.3-7.5; PDF p. 16, Supporting Information). The PDF has no embedded files, and no matching supplement was found in the local literature directory or screening tree. During reconciliation, urllib requests to the Wiley full article and Crossref DOI API, using User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, both failed with WinError 10013 (socket access blocked).
Possible overlap with c471 is flagged in the reconciled screening form. Participant reuse and independence remain unconfirmed; no shared-person count is assumed.
Lottery allocation probabilities or slot configuration are not reported, despite explicit individual random assignment (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1).
